analysis.title: Early Morning Reid - Macro Strategy
key_insights: Ahead of the Fed decision (6pm London) and Microsoft and Alphabet earnings after the US close, the Nasdaq (+1.18%) and S&P 500 (+0.60%) rose for a second day. Asia extended the tech optimism after SK Hynix results.

DB economists expect the Fed to hold rates, with futures pricing less than a 10% chance of a hike. They expect a hawkish message from Chair Warsh and see 50bp of further hikes across December and March.

DB economists think Warsh is likely to say that tighter financial conditions are not a substitute for rate hikes. The statement itself is expected to change only a little, and dissents to a hold are possible.

US data yesterday was on balance firmer than expected. Conference Board consumer confidence rebounded to 91.7 in October from 81.0 expected, and ADP showed private job gains averaging 16.75k a week in the 4 weeks to October 10.
The 10yr Treasury yield rose 1.0bp to 5.00% yesterday and is another 2.3bps higher overnight. The 2yr led the move, up 1.9bps.

Computer and related products new orders rose 3% m/m in the September durable goods report, putting annual growth at +26.7% y/y, the highest since 1997. Headline durable goods rose 1.8% against 1.9% expected.

The Philly semiconductor index rose 3.60% and the Mag-7 rose 0.94%. CoreWeave gained 7.94%, Broadcom 4.00% and Nvidia 0.90%. Today's Alphabet and Microsoft earnings are called the true test of the tech rally.
SK Hynix reported Q3 net profit that tripled from a year earlier and rose 9.84%. KOSPI is up 6.80% and Nasdaq futures are up 0.35%.

Brent fell 1.67% to $113.88 yesterday, then rose about 1.5% overnight to $115.59 after the WSJ reported the US warned Gulf states to prepare for a short, intense campaign against Iran after the midterms.

Iran's Supreme Leader restated Iran's conditions for ending the war. Iran met Saudi Arabia, Türkiye and Pakistan on Monday, and Saudi Aramco is offering spot cargoes to European buyers for this month and next.

Israel's election is too close to call. Two exit polls show the Netanyahu bloc and the Eizenkot-led opposition at about 51 seats each, short of the 61 needed. Prediction markets see no successful government formation as the most likely outcome. Turnout was 77.7%, the highest since 1999.

The euro fell 0.44% against the dollar for a fifth straight session to a 17-month low of 1.1125. DB's euro area surprise indicator turned negative for the first time since June, and the ECB Bank Lending Survey showed the tightest credit conditions since 2023.
France consumer confidence fell to 80 in October against 85 expected, the lowest since June 2013. The OAT-Bund spread widened 2.9bps to 156bps ahead of tomorrow's ECB decision.
European natural gas futures are up 0.84% and on course for a new post-2022 high. They fell 0.64% yesterday after Putin spoke with the Finnish president and the Norwegian PM.

Australian Q3 headline CPI rose 1.3% q/q against 1.2% expected, and trimmed mean rose 1.0% q/q, taking annual core inflation to 3.7% against 3.6% expected. A hike is now over 80% priced for next week's RBA meeting, and 10yr Aussie yields are up 5.6bps at 5.21%.
The RBNZ held its cash rate at 2.75% in a 4-3 vote, though a 25bp hike was more than 90% priced. The NZ dollar is down 1.2% against the US dollar. The bank signaled further tightening may be needed.
HSBC fell 5.42% after Q3 earnings missed estimates, which dragged the FTSE 100 down 0.75%.

market_movers.rationale: HSBC fell 5.42% after Q3 earnings fell short of estimates, making the FTSE 100 the only major European index to decline.

earnings_insights: HSBC Q3 earnings fell short of estimates (reported 10/28). The shares fell 5.42%.
SK Hynix Q3 net profit tripled from a year earlier (reported). The shares are up 9.84%.
Alphabet and Microsoft report after the US close today. They are expected to be the test of the tech rally.

risk_factors: The Fed's press conference could be more hawkish than expected.
Re-escalation with Iran after the US midterms could push oil higher.
Alphabet and Microsoft earnings could break the tech rally.
The euro area growth story is deteriorating, with consumer confidence and credit conditions weakening.
Israel's election may end without a government, which could lead to a new election.
vol_and_positioning: The euro's five-session slide to a 17-month low may partly reflect positioning, according to DB.
geopolitical: The WSJ reported the Trump administration told Gulf states to prepare for a short, intense military campaign against Iran after the midterms.
Israel's election is too close to call, and the outcome could matter for Iran policy if tensions re-escalate.
Iran's Supreme Leader restated the conditions for ending the war, and Iran met Saudi Arabia, Türkiye and Pakistan on Monday.
Putin spoke with the Finnish president and the Norwegian PM, his first call with Western European leaders in over a year. A localised temporary ceasefire took effect in Southern Ukraine.

tension_points.bull_case: Markets have held up with equities rising for a second day and futures pricing less than a 10% chance of a hike. Tighter financial conditions could ease the pressure for more hikes.
tension_points.bear_case: DB economists think recent inflation data support further tightening and expect 50bp of hikes across December and March. Warsh is likely to say that tighter financial conditions are not a substitute for hikes.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A Fed statement and press conference that signal tighter financial conditions are doing the work of hikes would undercut the hawkish call.
